signals.title: Display name contains a different email address
signals.explanation: The display name shows service@paypal.com, but the message is actually from finance.dept.2026@gmail.com. A mail client shows the display name, so the address a reader sees is not the address that sent this.
signals.advice: Treat the visible address as forged. Verify through a known-good channel.

signals.title: Display name claims a brand the domain does not belong to
signals.explanation: The display name claims PayPal, but the message was sent from gmail.com, which is a consumer mailbox provider. A brand does not contact customers from a personal mailbox.
signals.advice: Treat the branding as decoration. Verify through the brand's own app or site.

signals.title: Duplicate single-occurrence header
signals.explanation: These headers appear more than once: from. RFC 5322 permits one occurrence each. When a message carries two, the header a gateway validates and the header your mail client displays can be different ones, which is exactly what the technique exploits.
signals.advice: Compare the duplicated values. The one your client shows may not be the one that was validated.

signals.title: Message-ID is missing
signals.explanation: No Message-ID header is present. Mail clients and mail servers both set one as a matter of course, so its absence suggests the message was assembled by a script.
signals.advice: Weak on its own. Note it alongside the other findings.

signals.title: Authentication results are absent
signals.explanation: No Authentication-Results, Received-SPF or DKIM-Signature header is present, so SPF, DKIM and DMARC cannot be evaluated from this message alone.
signals.advice: Weak on its own. Note it alongside identity findings.

signals.title: Anchor text disagrees with the link target
signals.explanation: The visible text names paypal.com but the href points at billing-paypa1.example.
signals.advice: Trust the href, not the painted text. Do not visit either without verifying.

signals.title: Link puts a brand name on an unrelated domain
signals.explanation: The URL contains 'paypa1', which resembles PayPal, but billing-paypa1.example is not one of PayPal's domains.
signals.advice: The brand in the path is decoration. The registrable domain is what matters.
